clue.text: Old rubbish men spotted in the course of walk or fun run

indicators.note: something spotted in the course of a walk is seen partway along it, so these letters sit inside the word for walk

parts.note: to pace is to walk
tat is cheap rubbishy goods
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers or men

explanation.surface: Someone notices old rubbish and some men while out on a walk or a charity fun run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spotted in the course of' puts O + TAT + OR inside PACE. OR (other ranks) is the usual crossword abbreviation for men in the army.
explanation.definitionFit: A potato race is a light-hearted school sports-day event in which runners carry potatoes, an example of a fun run.

clue.text: Fairy bringing up vessel before king

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing something up means reading it from bottom to top, so the vessel's word is reversed

parts.note: a cup is a drinking vessel
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A fairy carries up a cup to present to the king.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'bringing up' means the vessel is read from the bottom upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Puck is the mischievous sprite of Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream, an example of a fairy.

clue.text: Rabbit to walk like a duck south of road junction

indicators.note: in a down entry, a part south of another is written below it, so the junction letter comes first

parts.note: a T-junction is a road junction, giving T
ducks waddle, moving with a side-to-side gait

explanation.surface: A rabbit has to waddle like a duck somewhere below a junction in the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rabbit' looks like the animal but is the British verb meaning to talk at length about nothing; its noun sense is nonsense chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang to rabbit (on) is to chatter idly, and its noun sense is talk of the same nonsensical kind, a synonym of drivel.

clue.text: What could be ever so true — art being seen as a valuable collection

indicators.note: asks what these letters might become when rearranged, signalling a new order

explanation.surface: A sincere remark that art can be considered a precious hoard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What could be' tells you to rearrange EVER SO TRUE plus ART.
explanation.definitionFit: Treasure trove is a hoard of valuables found hidden, a cache of precious items whose owner is unknown.

clue.text: Put down attendee at conference wanting new leader

indicators.note: wanting a new leader means the opening letter of the attendee's word must be swapped for a different one

parts.note: a delegate attends a conference on behalf of others

explanation.surface: A conference delegate is being snubbed because the group wants fresh leadership.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting new leader' replaces the first letter, D, of DELEGATE with R.
explanation.definitionFit: To relegate is to demote or consign to a lower position, which is one sense of putting down.

clue.text: A saint in church group

indicators.note: one word placed in another, so the A and saint letters go inside the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A saint belongs to a church congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: CE (Church of England) holds A + ST.
explanation.definitionFit: A caste is a hereditary social class or stratum, as in the Hindu system, so a social group.

clue.text: Fellow presenting information on time

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A man giving out information about the time.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British informal for information ('the gen'). Here 'on' just places GEN on top of T.
explanation.definitionFit: Gent, short for gentleman, is an informal word for a man, synonym of chap.

clue.text: Enduring out in space, learn to adapt

parts.note: ET, the extraterrestrial, comes from out in space

indicators.note: adapting a word alters it, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Instructions to survive in space: learn to adapt.
explanation.walkthrough: ET (the film alien) is followed by ERNAL, the rearranged LEARN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something eternal lasts forever, so it is everlasting and enduring.

clue.text: Opportunist who looks after the enemy?

definitions.text: Opportunist who looks after the enemy?

parts.words: Opportunist who looks after the enemy?
parts.note: the enemy is a jokey name for time, so one who looks after it is a server of time; such a person adapts to whatever suits the moment

explanation.surface: A turncoat who tends to the needs of the opposing side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The enemy' is a stock phrase for time ("What's the enemy?" = what time is it?), so a carer for the enemy serves time.
explanation.definitionFit: A timeserver adapts opinions to the prevailing fashion for personal gain, a self-serving opportunist.

clue.text: What is long and yellow with no tail?

indicators.note: a tail is the end, so the last letter of the cowardly word is dropped

parts.note: yellow means cowardly, as does craven

explanation.surface: A riddle about something long and yellow, like a banana missing its tip.
explanation.walkthrough: The riddle invites thoughts of bananas; in fact 'long' and 'yellow' are a verb and an adjective. CRAVEN loses its final N.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to yearn for it, desire it intensely.

clue.text: Odd male entertaining a European that is very bright

indicators.note: one who entertains a guest takes them in, so the remaining letters go inside
odd means strange or irregular, so the letters are put in an unusual order

parts.note: a Serb is a European from Serbia

explanation.surface: A strange man hosting a dazzling European visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd' rearranges the male letters into LEAM, and 'entertaining' takes the a-plus-European piece in after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A laser beam is an intensely concentrated ray of light, something extremely bright.

clue.text: Symbols of the past to be reckoned with

definitions.text: Symbols of the past to be reckoned with

parts.words: Symbols of the past to be reckoned with
parts.note: symbols from ancient Rome that were used for counting or reckoning, like I, V and X

explanation.surface: Relics of history that still demand attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To be reckoned with' looks like the idiom for something formidable; here it is literal: things you calculate with.
explanation.definitionFit: Letters such as X and V are the ancient Roman number signs, old symbols used for calculating.

clue.text: Greediest man's involved in arguments

indicators.note: involved means complicated or twisted, so the letters are tangled into another order

explanation.surface: A very greedy man gets caught up in quarrels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges all the letters of GREEDIEST MAN'S.
explanation.definitionFit: Disagreements are quarrels or rows, the sense of arguments as disputes.

clue.text: No smart set — jumbled collection of various items

indicators.note: jumbled means mixed up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Not a fashionable crowd, but a jumble of odds and ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumbled' rearranges NO SMART SET.
explanation.definitionFit: An assortment is a miscellaneous mix of different kinds of things, a medley.

clue.text: Something in soap is given attention in the country

indicators.note: one word placed within another, so the attention letters go inside the country word

parts.note: a state is a nation or country
to give ear is to pay attention

explanation.surface: A soap opera storyline gets national attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soap' suggests TV drama; it is the washing kind, and the answer is a chemical in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stearate is a salt of stearic acid; sodium stearate is a main ingredient of ordinary soap.

clue.text: One with inclination to go to river?

definitions.text: One with inclination to go to river?

indicators.note: one part goes to another, joining it at the end

parts.note: an angle is an inclination or slope

explanation.surface: Someone who feels like heading off to the riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inclination' reads as desire, but it is a slope: ANGLE, plus R.
explanation.definitionFit: A fisherman with rod and line naturally heads to a river, so the whole clue describes one.

clue.text: Creatures making bloke rested, we hear

indicators.note: signals that the phrase is to be heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: a bloke is a man, and rested means at ease, giving man at ease

explanation.surface: Creatures that turn a man into a lazybones, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' means MAN AT EASE spoken aloud gives the answer's sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Manatees, or sea cows, are large plant-eating marine mammals, an example of creatures.

clue.text: Attacks on TV the ultimate in nastiness?

parts.note: a TV is a television set

indicators.note: the ultimate is the last, so take the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Is the latest TV show the last word in nastiness?
explanation.walkthrough: ON + SET (TV set) + S, the last letter of 'nastiness'.
explanation.definitionFit: An onset is an assault or attack, as in an onset of enemy troops; the word is plural here.

clue.text: Heavenly body doesn't need a body-building chemical

indicators.note: what is not needed is left out, so the letter is removed

parts.note: an asteroid is a small rocky body orbiting the sun

explanation.surface: A heavenly body has no need of a muscle-building drug.
explanation.walkthrough: ASTEROID drops its A.
explanation.definitionFit: Anabolic steroids are drugs used to build muscle, so a steroid is a muscle-building compound.

clue.text: Be full of sickness, having dry bread

indicators.note: a word full of something holds it inside, so the other pieces go between its letters

parts.note: ague is a fever with shivering, a sickness
TT, teetotal, means abstaining from alcohol, i.e. dry

explanation.surface: Someone sick and gorging on stale bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dry' means teetotal here, abbreviated TT; 'full of' has the clue's opening word hold the illness and that abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A baguette is a long thin French loaf, an example of bread.

clue.text: Tube to deter travelling around?

indicators.note: letters travelling around move about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A question whether the Tube puts people off travelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tube' suggests the London Underground; it is a vacuum tube. TO DETER is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetrode is a thermionic valve with four electrodes, a type of electronic vacuum tube.

clue.text: Possibly vote in haste, eh? This brings a negative decision

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A rushed vote in Parliament leads to a refusal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges VOTE IN HASTE, EH. The answer is what the Speaker of the House of Commons announces when a vote is lost.
explanation.definitionFit: This parliamentary announcement declares that those voting against have won, so a motion is defeated.

clue.text: Storyteller's first yarn lacking originality

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, taken from storyteller

parts.note: a yarn is a story or tale

explanation.surface: A writer's debut story turns out to be derivative.
explanation.walkthrough: S from 'Storyteller's' + TALE.
explanation.definitionFit: Stale ideas are hackneyed and overused, so they lack originality.

clue.text: Money HQ about to be demolished

indicators.note: something demolished is knocked down and gone, so these letters are removed

parts.note: headquarters is the centre of operations
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A firm's headquarters is set for demolition to raise funds.
explanation.walkthrough: CENTRE loses RE (about, as in a letter heading).
explanation.definitionFit: A cent is a small coin worth a hundredth of a dollar or euro, a unit of money.

clue.text: Clear individual pursuing old lover, gaining speed

indicators.note: pursuing means following behind, so this part comes after the old lover

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
one means a single individual
rate means pace or speed

explanation.surface: Someone chasing a former partner, picking up pace, is found innocent.
explanation.walkthrough: EX, then ONE (pursuing it), then RATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To exonerate is to absolve someone of blame, i.e. to clear their name.

clue.text: Fuss with Religious Education and Worship

parts.note: ado is fuss or bother
RE is the school subject Religious Education

explanation.surface: School religion lessons and worship cause a lot of fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the British school subject Religious Education.
explanation.definitionFit: To adore is to love deeply or to revere as divine, synonym of venerate.

clue.text: One waited for returning? No good fussing

indicators.note: no means without, so the letter for good is dropped
something returning comes back, so the waited-for name is read backwards

parts.note: Godot is the character waited for in Beckett's play Waiting for Godot

explanation.surface: Is someone awaited coming back? It is pointless making a fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns GODOT into TODOG; 'No good' removes the G. Godot never arrives in Beckett's play.
explanation.definitionFit: A to-do is a commotion or fuss, and the noun fussing means the same agitated bustle.

clue.text: Determined person not getting on is needing shelter

indicators.note: a word not getting something goes without it, so those letters are removed

parts.note: taken as written
a tent is a portable shelter

explanation.surface: A resolute person, unable to get on, needs a place to stay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not getting' strips ON from PERSON to leave PERS, then IS + TENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Persistent describes someone who keeps going despite difficulty, synonym of dogged or resolute.
